pass_b_english: When all things on earth have been restored to their rightful state, with death and Satan, who tyrannized over them, having been rendered powerless, the Son will again have the superiority of authority over all things in the future age.

The prophet Isaiah prophesies beforehand, saying that the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those on the earth will rejoice, for the dew from God is a healing for them, symbolizing the life-giving energy of God, by which he grants being to non-beings and well-being to those already existing (Isaiah 26:19).
All things consist in God, just as they were also brought into being through him.

David also sings about the things on earth to the Savior God of all, saying that when God opens his hand, all things will be filled with goodness, but when he turns away his face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit, and they will fail, and they will return to their dust; you will send out your spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth (Psalm 104:29-30).

Human nature suffered the turning away of the divine face in Adam due to transgression, and therefore, it has been almost completely destroyed and troubled, and it has returned to its own dust, and it has been led down to death and corruption.
With the Only-Begotten Word of God dwelling among us and the Holy Spirit's presence enriching our lives, we are undergoing a transformation, returning to our original state and being rebuilt.
This is because we have been called to a new life, one that escapes the power of death.

The apostle Paul, in his wisdom, testifies to this truth, saying that if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, He will give life to our mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in us (Romans 8:11).
When Christ rose from the dead, conquering the power of death and becoming the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, it is only logical that we will follow in His footsteps.

If someone were to carefully examine the works of God and the origin of each thing, seeking to thoroughly understand the manner of each creation and the beginning of each generation, they would never finish asking how this is possible.
For instance, one might wonder how heaven was made, from what material or where, what foundation it has, or how the earth was created and divided, or how the sun, moon, and stars were formed.
Similarly, the creation of humanity is a profound mystery, as it involves the transformation of dust into flesh and bones.
If we cannot understand the reason behind each of these creations, we risk abolishing the fact that they were created at all.
Doubting the resurrection after Christ's resurrection is a sign of foolishness, ignorance, and arrogance, as it questions the power of God's works.
Asking how God's works are done or with what body the dead will rise is also foolish.
Some people claim that the soul preexisted and was bound to the body as a form of punishment, but this idea undermines the concept of creation and the purpose of God's work.

The Lord rose from the dead in the same body, as the prophet Isaiah said, 'The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those on the earth will rejoice; for the dew from you is a healing for them' (Isaiah 26:19).

As David said, 'When you open your hand, all things will be filled with goodness; but when you turn away your face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit, and they will fail, and they will return to their dust; you will send out your spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth' (Psalm 104:29-30).
Paul also said, 'If the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, He will give life to our mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in us' (Romans 8:11).
